questions.question: How sensitive is the commodity derivatives book to a 10% drop in commodity prices?
questions.answer: Net unrealized losses would rise by $27.4 million, generally offset by lower costs for the underlying commodity purchases.
questions.quote: assuming a 10% decrease in the underlying commodity price, would have increased our net unrealized losses in 2020 by $27.4 million

questions.question: How much goodwill was on the balance sheet at the end of 2020?
questions.answer: Goodwill had a net book value of $1,988.2 million at December 31, 2020, with no impairment charges.
questions.quote: At December 31, 2020, the net book value of our goodwill totaled $1,988.2 million.

questions.question: Who helps management estimate fair values of assets picked up in acquisitions?
questions.answer: They normally use a third-party valuation specialist to estimate fair values of acquired tangible and intangible assets.
questions.quote: we normally obtain the assistance of a third-party valuation specialist in estimating fair values of tangible and intangible assets

questions.question: What happens to pension expense and the pension liability if the discount rate falls by 1 point?
questions.answer: Annual pension expense would rise about $7 million and the year-end 2020 pension liability would rise about $108 million.
questions.quote: A 100 basis point decrease (increase) in the weighted-average pension discount rate would increase (decrease) annual net periodic pension benefit expense by approximately $7 million and the December 31, 2020 pension liability would increase by approximately $108 million

questions.question: Why did working capital turn into a source of cash in 2019?
questions.answer: Higher collections before year-end 2019, timing of vendor and supplier payments, and higher accrued incentive compensation paid in early 2020.
questions.quote: This $164 million fluctuation was mainly driven by higher cash receipts prior to year-end 2019, the timing of vendor and supplier payments, as well as higher accrued incentive compensation

questions.question: What caused operating cash flow to fall in 2020?
questions.answer: Working capital used $166 million, mainly from a bigger U.S. inventory build and higher receivables on stronger U.S. seasonal sales.
questions.quote: This $226 million fluctuation was mainly driven by a higher year-over-year build up of U.S. inventories to satisfy product requirements and maintain sufficient levels to accommodate customer requirements, as well as an increase in cash used by accounts receivable

questions.question: How much did North America segment profit grow in 2020 and what drove it?
questions.answer: Up $195.9 million or 9.2%, on price realization and volume gains, partly offset by COVID-related supply chain costs.
questions.quote: Our North America segment income increased $195.9 million or 9.2% in 2020 compared to 2019, primarily due to favorable price realization and volume increases

questions.question: How much did diluted EPS grow in 2020?
questions.answer: Diluted EPS rose $0.65, or 11.9%, versus 2019.
questions.quote: EPS-diluted increased $0.65, or 11.9%, in 2020 compared with 2019

questions.question: Why did advertising spend decline in 2020?
questions.answer: Advertising and consumer marketing fell 2.0% on media cost efficiencies and COVID-related brand investment cuts in International and Other.
questions.quote: Total advertising and related consumer marketing expenses decreased 2.0% driven by media cost efficiencies and select brand investment optimization related to COVID-19 in International and Other segments.

questions.question: What was the operating margin in 2020 versus the prior year?
questions.answer: Operating profit margin was 21.9% in 2020, up from 20.0% in 2019.
questions.quote: Operating profit margin | 21.9% | 20.0% | 20.8%

questions.question: How is the Pirate's Booty acquisition performing against the original deal plan?
questions.answer: It is tracking ahead of the strategic plan, as referenced in the prepared remarks.
questions.quote: Pirate's Booty is tracking ahead of your strategic plans

questions.question: How big a piece of cost of goods is freight?
questions.answer: Freight is roughly 10% of COGS; rising rates aren't a material impact yet because of contracts.
questions.quote: it's roughly 10% of COGS overall

questions.question: How much share did they gain in convenience stores in Q3?
questions.answer: About 120 basis points of share gains in the C-store channel in the third quarter.
questions.quote: we have share gains of about 120 basis points in Q3 in that channel

questions.question: Will 2021 gross margin be driven more by pricing or by volume?
questions.answer: More by volume than price mix next year, along with cocoa crop effects and the ongoing productivity goal.
questions.quote: we'll have a little bit more volume-driven than price-driven mix driving gross margin next year

questions.question: Which new product launches is management most excited about this year?
questions.answer: A Reese's cup with pretzels, a range of Kit Kat flavors, and small-scale Reese's snack cakes.
questions.quote: the reese pretzel product a reese cup with pretzels in it we've had a a range of kit kat flavors

questions.question: What does management expect from the promotional environment through Q4 and into 2021?
questions.answer: No significant change in promotional activity; none was seen this year and none is expected going forward.
questions.quote: we don't see any significant change relative to promotional activity.

questions.question: After a strong start and softer finish, where was the category's total season expected to end up?
questions.answer: Down mid-single digits for the category overall, implying sharp late-season declines in upcoming retail data.
questions.quote: finished down mid-single digits for the category

questions.question: What did the analyst credit for the unusually strong early Halloween sales?
questions.answer: Retailer merchandising programs that started bigger and earlier than usual.
questions.quote: a big part of that is due to the merchandising programs that retailers had. It seems like they started bigger and earlier than they usually do.

questions.question: How does Halloween sell-through affect the start of the holiday selling season?
questions.answer: Strong Halloween sell-through clears shelf space so holiday product goes on the floor sooner, giving holiday a fast start.
questions.quote: A strong Halloween sell-through really helps us because it helps us get that fast start to holiday because it clears the space to be able to put holiday on the floor.

questions.question: What risk did analysts raise about whether U.S. chocolate share gains will hold in 2021?
questions.answer: If gains came from competitors' supply chain breakdowns or slower adaptation, competitors could win some share back in 2021.
questions.quote: if there is a supply chain breakdown or lack of adaptability by a competitor, maybe that will represent share gains that they can reverse somewhat in 21.

questions.question: How did operating cash flow end up positive in 2020 despite the net loss?
questions.answer: $16.6 million of operating cash flow, as $24.9 million of non-cash expenses more than offset the $9.4 million net loss.
questions.quote: net cash provided by operating activities of $16.6 million was primarily due to a net loss of $9.4 million being more than offset by non-cash expenses of $24.9 million

questions.question: Why did interest expense drop so much in 2020?
questions.answer: Lower rates and a shorter term on revolving debt, with all debt paid off on July 24, 2020.
questions.quote: primarily as a result of lower interest rates and a shorter term on our outstanding revolving short-term debt as we paid in full all of our debt on July 24, 2020

questions.question: How much did revenue grow in 2020?
questions.answer: Revenue grew 38% to $116.2 million from $84.1 million in 2019.

questions.question: What typically happens to demand and pricing in a semiconductor downturn?
questions.answer: Demand falls, capacity and inventories run high, and average selling prices erode faster.
questions.quote: Downturns in the semiconductor industry have been characterized by diminished product demand, production overcapacity, high inventory levels, and accelerated erosion of average selling prices.

questions.question: How could pandemic stress in credit markets hurt the company's funding?
questions.answer: Weaker credit markets could limit access to outside financing for operations and capital expenditures.
questions.quote: the deterioration in credit markets could limit our ability to obtain external financing to fund our operations and capital expenditures

questions.question: Why is earthquake risk relevant to operations?
questions.answer: Headquarters and some suppliers and foundry vendors sit in active earthquake zones or areas prone to outages and disasters.
questions.quote: Our corporate headquarters and some of our suppliers and foundry vendors are located in areas that are in active earthquake zones

questions.question: Why might patent infringement claims against the company increase?
questions.answer: Its higher profile and visibility as a public company may draw more infringement allegations from others.
questions.quote: particularly as a public company with an increased profile and visibility, receive communications from others alleging our infringement

questions.question: How large are the NOL carryforwards as of year-end 2020?
questions.answer: About $201.5 million federal and $64.0 million state net operating loss carryforwards.
questions.quote: U.S. federal and state net operating loss (“NOL”) carryforwards of approximately $201.5 million and $64.0 million, respectively

questions.question: How could future fundraising affect existing shareholders?
questions.answer: Issuing equity or convertible debt could significantly dilute holders, and new securities could rank senior to common stock.
questions.quote: If we raise additional funds by issuing equity securities or convertible debt, stockholders may experience significant dilution of their ownership interest

questions.question: What's the impact if a fab, assembly or test partner ends its relationship with the company?
questions.answer: Shipping on time and in required quantities would suffer, potentially causing unexpected sales declines and lost customers.
questions.quote: our ability to ship our solutions to our customers on time and in the quantity required would be adversely affected

questions.question: How much has the customer base grown over the last five years?
questions.answer: From about 2,000 customers five years ago to roughly five times that today, mostly smaller customers reached through the channel.
questions.quote: five years ago we were addressing about 2,000 customers. Today we're about 5x that, maybe a little bit more.

questions.question: What's the gross margin outlook for the first half of 2021?
questions.answer: Margins should dip slightly in the first half on heavier volume weighting, then strengthen considerably in the back half.
questions.quote: I would actually expect gross margins to pull back just a little bit in the first half of next year

questions.question: How should analysts model gross margin for next year?
questions.answer: Model the full-year margin as a whole; the back half will be higher than the first half.
questions.quote: I would model gross margins for what you think it would be for the year in total.

questions.question: How long does it take resonator design wins to turn into meaningful revenue?
questions.answer: Slower than clocking: the lead time to meaningful revenue is easily twice as long, especially for SoC vendor design-ins.
questions.quote: the gestation period for that, for meaningful revenue, is easily twice as long as the clocking business.

questions.question: When was the Cascade clock IC expected to start contributing revenue?
questions.answer: Revenue was expected to begin in 2021 and ramp beyond that, per the analyst's recap of last quarter's announcement.
questions.quote: the Clock IC product that you expected revenue to really be a 2021 event beginning and then probably ramping beyond that

questions.question: What process nodes does the company use for its chips?
questions.answer: 180, 130 and 65 nanometer tape-outs, versus 7nm at other semiconductor companies, as an analog company.
questions.quote: we're doing 180, 130, 65 nanometer tape outs

questions.question: How long does management think the 5G infrastructure buildout will last?
questions.answer: Probably a five-to-seven-year rollout, providing steady growth.
questions.quote: this is probably a five, seven-year rollout

questions.question: What new market is the Apex MEMS family moving the company into?
questions.answer: The resonator market.
questions.quote: with the recent introduction of the Apex MEMS family, you're moving into the resonator market

questions.question: How big is the serviceable addressable market today?
questions.answer: SAM is about $1.0 to $1.2 billion, under $2 billion, mostly in oscillators.
questions.quote: our SAM is still around a billion to a billion point two.

questions.question: How concentrated is the supply of ceramic packages for quartz timing parts?
questions.answer: Only two suppliers worldwide make them, and shortages sometimes occur.
questions.quote: Those quartz packaging, ceramic packages, come from only two people in the world, and sometimes there's a shortage.

questions.question: Who is responsible for monitoring commodity price, currency and interest rate risk?
questions.answer: The EVP and CFO, who reports to the CEO.
questions.quote: The Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, who reports to the Chief Executive Officer, monitors commodity price risk and risks resulting from foreign currency exchange rates and interest rates.

questions.question: What is management's position on the climate change lawsuits filed against oil and gas companies?
questions.answer: It considers them factually and legally meritless, an inappropriate way to address climate change, and will vigorously defend.
questions.quote: believes these lawsuits are factually and legally meritless and are an inappropriate vehicle to address the challenges associated with climate change and will vigorously defend against such lawsuits.

questions.question: What is the Moody's rating on the senior long-term debt?
questions.answer: A3 with a stable outlook, affirmed in October 2020.
questions.quote: Moody’s affirmed its rating of our senior long-term debt of “A3” with a “stable” outlook

questions.question: Why did earnings from the technology business fall in 2020?
questions.answer: Technology earnings fell $149 million, mainly due to lower licensing revenues.
questions.quote: Earnings from Technology decreased by $149 million in 2020 compared with 2019, primarily due to lower licensing revenues.

questions.question: What cost savings were announced alongside the Concho deal?
questions.answer: $350 million of annual savings by 2022, from organizational streamlining, a refocused exploration program and redundant combined G&A.
questions.quote: quantified $350 million of annual expense savings expected to be achieved by 2022

questions.question: How much liquidity did the company have at the end of 2020?
questions.answer: Over $12 billion: $3.0 billion cash, $3.6 billion short-term investments and $5.7 billion available under the credit facility.
questions.quote: We ended the year with over $12 billion of liquidity, comprised of $3.0 billion in cash and cash equivalents, $3.6 billion in short-term investments, and available borrowings under our credit facility of $5.7 billion.

questions.question: How could climate regulation hurt the business financially?
questions.answer: It could lower product demand, add taxes on products or operations, or require buying emission credits or cutting GHG emissions.
questions.quote: may adversely impact the demand for our products, impose taxes on our products or operations or require us to purchase emission credits or reduce emission of GHGs from our operations.

questions.question: Why might the company be disadvantaged against national oil companies?
questions.answer: State-owned companies may act on political or other motives with less focus on financial returns.
questions.quote: we may be at a competitive disadvantage when competing with state-owned companies if they are motivated by political or other factors in making their business decisions, with less emphasis on financial returns.

questions.question: How could prolonged low oil and gas prices affect DD&A?
questions.answer: Lower reserve estimates could raise the unit-of-production rate used for DD&A expense.
questions.quote: our reserve estimates may decrease further, which could incrementally increase the rate used to determine DD&A expense on our unit-of-production method properties.

questions.question: How does the company track diversity in its recruiting?
questions.answer: University dashboards track recruiting metrics like gender, ethnicity and acceptance rates, shared internally through D&I Dashboards.
questions.quote: We closely monitor recruitment metrics through our university dashboards in areas such as gender, ethnicity and university acceptance rates

questions.question: How would excess cash be returned if oil prices run above the mid-cycle price assumption?
questions.answer: Still evaluating options and open to all approaches; for now the dividend more than covers shareholder returns.
questions.quote: the dividend more than satisfies our return to shareholders.

questions.question: Why does management stress optimizing each asset across the portfolio?
questions.answer: Without optimizing across a diverse portfolio you don't capture diversification's value, so they aim to run every asset at its optimum.
questions.quote: if you're not optimizing across a diverse portfolio, then you're not maximizing the value that the diversification brings you.

questions.question: What signs did analysts point to that the oil cycle may be bottoming?
questions.answer: Industry consolidation, including the company's own Concho deal.
questions.quote: We've now seen what we think is a lot of the signs of a cycle coming to a bottom, if you like, with consolidation, yourselves being part of that.

questions.question: What options did the analyst raise for assets losing exploration and appraisal funding after the Concho deal?
questions.answer: Whether they simply return to the resource base or become more likely to be sold or otherwise monetized.
questions.quote: Do they just go back into the resource base, or is that something that maybe becomes more likely to be disposed of, you know, monetized in a different way?

questions.question: When will 2021 capex guidance for the combined company be given?
questions.answer: Not until sometime after the Concho transaction closes.
questions.quote: you shouldn't expect us to communicate 2021 capital guidance, certainly for the combined company, until sometime after the transaction closes.

questions.question: What's the status of the planned Alaska sell-down?
questions.answer: Still expected, but timing slowed until uncertainties are resolved; Willow's timing isn't contingent on it.
questions.quote: we're still anticipating that we will do a sell down in Alaska. We just slowed the timing of that down until we get some of these uncertainties resolved.

questions.question: What level of equity affiliate distributions should be modeled for next year at strip prices?
questions.answer: Roughly $600 to $800 million, with APLNG distributions heavier in Q2 and Q4.
questions.quote: the range of $600 to $800 million from equity affiliates at those kind of pricing

questions.question: How could ConocoPhillips' marketing improve realizations on Concho's production?
questions.answer: Concho sells at the wellhead, while ConocoPhillips sells further down the value chain to get better realized prices.
questions.quote: Concho typically sells their product to the wellhead. We sell further down the value chain to improve realisation.

questions.question: What's the pro forma cash flow for the combined company at $40 oil?
questions.answer: Roughly $7.5 to $7.8 billion at $40 a barrel, including the full $350 million of expected cost savings.
questions.quote: it would imply somewhere between seven and a half and seven eight at $40 a barrel.

questions.question: What should be used as the starting point for 2021 capital and production?
questions.answer: Fourth-quarter 2020 levels are the new baseline, subject to ongoing monitoring of market conditions.
questions.quote: you should take the fourth quarter as the new baseline for 21 capital and production
